question: A team is designing the error payload that subagents return to a coordinator when a tool call fails. Which set of fields best supports intelligent coordinator recovery decisions?
options: A) A free-text log excerpt of the subagent's entire internal reasoning trace leading right up to the failure
B) Failure type, the action that was attempted, any partial results gathered, and alternative approaches to try next
C) A single numeric error code mapped to an internal lookup table that only the platform team is allowed to maintain
D) A retry count and a timestamp, since the coordinator can infer the rest from prior attempts alone
correct_answers: B) Failure type, the action that was attempted, any partial results gathered, and alternative approaches to try next
explanations: A full reasoning trace is noisy and unstructured; the coordinator would have to parse free text to extract the same information that structured fields would provide directly.
Correct. These four elements together let a coordinator judge whether the failure is worth retrying, whether existing partial results are usable, and what alternative path might succeed.
A bare numeric code requires the coordinator to look up meaning elsewhere and still lacks partial results or alternatives, so it cannot drive a recovery decision on its own.
Retry count and timestamp say nothing about why the failure happened, what was attempted, or whether partial results exist, so the coordinator still cannot make an informed recovery choice.
